questions.qtext:
Two transactions are "not-interleaved" in a schedule if every action of one transaction precedes every action of the other.
We say that a transaction $T$ precedes a transaction $U$ in a schedule $S$ if they are not interleaved, and all actions of $T$ precedes all actions of $U$ in $S.$

Note that if $T$ and $U$ are the Only transactions in $S$, then saying $T$ precedes $U$ is the same as saying that $S$ is the serial schedule $(T, U).$

However, if $S$ involves transactions other than $T$ and $U,$ then $S$ might not be a serial schedule, in fact, because of the effect of other transactions, $S$ might not even be conflict-serializable.

Consider a conflict-serializable schedule $S$ in which transactions $\mathrm{T1}$ and $T2$ are not interleaved in $S,$ and $T1$ precedes $T2$ in $S.$ The Schedule $S$ may include more than $2$ transactions.

Which of the following must be true for $S?$

options.text: In any serial schedule conflict equivalent to $\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{T} 1$ precedes $T2.$
In any serial schedule conflict equivalent to $\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{T} 2$ precedes $T1.$
There exists at least one serial schedule conflict equivalent to $S$ in which $T1$ precedes $T2.$
None of the above is necessarily true.
